Dungru.description: A local boy who enjoys singing and playing instruments; he witnesses a mysterious accident involving a stranger falling down a hill.

Shyam Gurung.description: The local greengrocer who owns an instrument that Dungru borrows.

Joe.description: One of the foreign men camping near the spring, who helps Dungru with the injured man.

Mark.description: A member of the group of foreign men; he has studied medicine in Minnesota and checks the injured man's pulse.

Dennis.description: Another member of the group of foreign men camping near the spring.

Bruce.description: Another member of the group of foreign men camping near the spring.

Minnesota.description: A state in the United States; mentioned as the place where Mark studied medicine.

Kathmandu.description: The capital city of Nepal, referenced as the location of the nearest hospital.

Tapesh.description: The narrator of the story and Feluda's younger cousin and assistant.

Puri.description: A coastal city in the Indian state of Orissa, famous for its beaches and temples.

skylab.description: Refers to the American space station that fell to Earth in 1979, causing public anxiety worldwide.

coolie.description: A manual laborer or porter, especially one who carries luggage at railway stations in India.

Sikkim.description: A state in northeastern India, mentioned as another possible place D.G. Sen visited.

Sen Perfumers.description: The family business founded by S.N. Sen, once known for producing Sensational Essences.

Madhupur.description: A town in India, referenced as one of the locations where the Sen family owned property.

koftas.description: A type of Indian dish consisting of spiced balls, often made from vegetables or meat.

paan.description: A traditional Indian preparation made of betel leaf filled with various ingredients, often chewed for its flavor.

Charminar.description: A popular brand of Indian cigarettes.

puthi.description: Ancient manuscripts or scrolls, traditionally written on palm leaves or paper before the printing press era.

Rupchand Singh.description: The deceased man found on the beach, identified by his driving licence.

Lokenath.description: A servant at D.G. Sen's house, mentioned as being absent when called.

Dalai Lama.description: The spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism, who fled to India in 1959.

Kashmiri.description: Relating to Kashmir, a region in northern India, referenced in the description of a table.

Godrej.description: A well-known Indian brand, here referring to the manufacturer of the safes in Mr Sen's room.

Sanskrit.description: An ancient classical language of India, in which some manuscripts are written.

Bengali.description: A language spoken in the Indian state of West Bengal and Bangladesh.

India.description: The country in which the story is set.

Namaskar.description: A traditional Indian greeting, similar to 'hello' or 'greetings'.

ayurveda.description: An ancient Indian system of medicine based on natural and holistic approaches.

Railway Hotel.description: A hotel near the beach in Puri, popular among visitors.

Goa.description: A state on the western coast of India, famous for its beaches.

Miami.description: A city in the United States, known for its beaches.

Nice.description: A city in France, renowned for its Mediterranean coastline.

Himalayas.description: A major mountain range in Asia, home to some of the world's highest peaks.

bindi.description: A decorative dot worn on the forehead, traditionally by Hindu women, but here used to describe a mole's appearance.

paise.description: A subunit of the Indian rupee, with 100 paise making one rupee.

Mr Sarkar.description: A resident of Meher Ali Road, whose whereabouts are being investigated.

Jagannath.description: A famous Hindu temple in Puri, Odisha, dedicated to Lord Jagannath.

Konark.description: A town in Odisha, India, known for the Sun Temple and its iconic stone carvings.

New Guinea.description: An island in the southwestern Pacific, mentioned in relation to the reptile Taratua.

Libra.description: An astrological sign, referenced during the astrologer's reading.

Vande Mataram.description: A patriotic Indian slogan and song, referenced during a vision of the past.

lungi.description: A traditional garment worn around the waist, common in South Asia.

kurta.description: A loose, collarless shirt worn in South Asia.

divan.description: A long, low sofa or couch, often without a back or arms.

Pokhra.description: A city in Nepal, known for its natural beauty, mentioned as a travel destination.

souffle.description: A light, fluffy baked dish, usually served as a dessert.

gout.description: A medical condition characterized by painful inflammation of the joints.

New Hotel.description: Another hotel in Puri, where Lalmohan Babu's driver is accommodated.

Bhubaneshwar.description: The capital city of Odisha, India, famous for its ancient temples.

Statesman.description: An English-language newspaper published in India.

Jagannath Express.description: A train running from Calcutta (Kolkata) to Puri.

Mystery Magazine.description: A fictional or real magazine featuring detective stories, referenced in the story.

Bhaskareshwar.description: A temple in Bhubaneshwar, part of the city's temple heritage.

Michaelangelo.description: Refers to Michelangelo, the famous Italian Renaissance artist.

Da Vinci.description: Refers to Leonardo da Vinci, the renowned Italian polymath.

veranda.description: A roofed, open-air porch or gallery attached to the outside of a building, common in South Asian architecture.

chappals.description: A type of open-toed sandal commonly worn in India.

Ramai.description: A Nulia boy with a red scarf, encountered by Feluda and his companions on the beach.

Signal.description: A popular Indian brand of toothpaste, recognized by its red-and-white packaging.

America.description: Referenced as the country Dr Senapati visited to bring back medicine.

Keonjhargarh.description: A place the characters are invited to visit, possibly a wildlife area.

Hotchkick.description: A fictional or possibly real suspense film or character, used for comparison.

kurta-pajamas.description: A traditional Indian outfit consisting of a long tunic (kurta) and loose trousers (pajamas).

Pragya Paramita.description: A twelfth-century manuscript, highly valuable and central to the plot.

Shanta Bhavan.description: A hospital in Patan, near Kathmandu, where Mr Sen was treated.
